text.text: SO-101 Dinner Table: a scored bimanual benchmark
Bimanual VLA Manipulation with Multi-Modal Reasoning — Setting Up a Dinner Table
AI Infra Summit Hackathon · Intel Physical AI Online Challenge · lablab.ai
—  A randomized dual-SO-101 dinner-table task in MuJoCo
—  Five ordered success predicates, scored per seed
—  A scorer controlled both ways, so its number can be falsified
0 / 50 with the arms held in the home pose  ·  task success 0 / 10
The problem this entry actually attacks
A bimanual demo video is easy to make and impossible to check.
—  Did the result survive a new random seed, or was it one lucky run?
—  Would the scorer have fired anyway with the arms held still?
—  Which of the five steps in the instruction actually happened?
—  Was it one arm doing everything, with the second along for the ride?

Teams training manipulation policies for the low-cost open arms this track names report success rates on environments nobody else can rerun. So this entry built the measuring instrument first, and reports what the instrument says — including the zeros.
Two SO-101 arms — five positioning joints and a parallel jaw each
A cabinet with a prismatic drawer holding the fork and the spoon
Plate, mug and bottle on the table
Object geometry, mass, friction, lighting, background and placement vary per seed
Rejection-sampled: every episode is reachable and never blocks the drawer
Five ordered sub-goals: drawer, fork, spoon, plate, mug
Also logs order, arm, hand-off and drops
Open the top drawer, pick up the fork and the spoon and lay them either side of the place setting, put the plate on the mat, then set the mug down to the right of the plate.
The number ships with its own falsifier
Same seeds. Same scorer bytes. Only the controller differs.
Any sub-goal that fired with the arms held still would mean the scorer produced the result, not the controller. None fires.
A scorer that can only say yes proves nothing. Every predicate is driven from both sides: a state that must score, and a state that must not. Both are in the repository and both run in seconds.
Results, per sub-goal — including the zeros
What the run does not show
in-order prefix 1 of 5 on every seed
both arms touched an object on 10 / 10 seeds
all 10 recorded hand-offs are the two arms taking the drawer handle in turn, not an object

The plate is hooked by its rim and dragged flat, not picked and placed: it is 94–115 mm across the ten evaluation seeds, wider than the jaw can both clear and close on. The scorer does not ask how the plate reached the mat. This deck does.
Worst IK residual over the ten rollouts: 361.9 mm across 1,810 planned moves — waypoints the arm never reaches are the open defect this entry has not fixed.
Robustness: one controller, ten random seeds

Robustness is evidenced for the two steps that fire and for nothing else: the drawer on 10 / 10 seeds and the plate on 4 / 10. There is still no performance on the other three sub-goals to be robust about. Placement randomization is rejection-sampled, so a failed episode is a controller failure and never an impossible scene.
The demo video covers the same 10 seeds and is captioned frame by frame from the live predicate state, so it cannot claim more than the evaluation reports · sha256 eea237a0b41a…
One overhead frame in, table layout out
—  80 epochs; the three splits are seed-disjoint by construction
—  18.41 mm validation, 2.39 mm on the ten evaluation seeds
Two controls it has to beat
no-vision baseline 84.36 mm  ·  shuffled labels 106.91 mm
Stated plainly: this is perception, not a policy. It outputs scene state, not actions, and it is not in the control loop — the controller still reads privileged simulator state.
Wiring it in is the next step, and until it is taken this entry claims nothing for the VLA criterion.
Exported IR, and what each precision costs
INT8 is 3.9× smaller than FP32 and costs 10.07 mm
—  async throughput at the plugin's own optimal request count
—  the execution precision the plugin actually chose
—  the model's task quality in millimetres
On this host, OpenVINO 2026.3.1: CPU/FP32 0.426 ms p50, 5,488 fps async.
The cost of INT8 is reported and not hidden — a control named reject_int8_is_free fails if INT8 is ever recorded as no worse than FP32.
Those latency numbers are not the measurement this track scores. The next slide says why, and what would fix it.
No Intel Core Ultra measurement exists here
The track asks for: Intel Core Ultra Series 2/3 with OpenVINO
two NVIDIA L40S, no Intel silicon, no NPU
on a Core Ultra Series 2/3 machine, NPU included

The accept path is tested without owning the hardware: the verdict function accepts 3 real Core Ultra part strings and rejects 4 non-Core-Ultra ones, including this host, a Xeon and a Core i9. So the branch that would report success is exercised, not merely the branch that refuses.

AMD numbers are not offered under an Intel heading. The report stamps itself, in the file, as not the required measurement — because a judge who cannot trust the small claims cannot check the large ones.
This entry is smaller than the track asks for, and exact about which parts are missing.
—  No learned policy: no VLA, no imitation learning, no language conditioning.
—  Task success 0 / 10 — the table has never been set.
—  Object hand-off only ever with the mug, on 5 / 10 seeds.
—  Perception is not in the control loop; the controller reads privileged simulator state.
—  No Intel Core Ultra measurement: NOT_THE_REQUIRED_MEASUREMENT.
—  The plate is dragged by its rim, not carried.
Every one of these is also stated in the repository README, in TECHNICAL_SUMMARY.md section 8 and in the submission text — and scripts/test_slides.py fails if this slide stops stating any of them.
Value: who it is for, and what would pay for it
Robotics teams training manipulation policies for low-cost open arms. Today they report success rates on environments nobody else can rerun.
The instrument, not the policy: a seeded, randomized, ordered-sub-goal task with a falsifier attached — cheap enough to run on a laptop.
A versioned open benchmark with hosted evaluation, so a team can quote a number it can defend. Sponsorship and private leaderboards follow that, not the other way round.

Market size is not estimated here, because nothing was measured that would support an estimate. None of the route above is built: there are no users and there is no revenue. It is the route, not a claim.
What exists today that another team could use: the scene, the randomizer, the scorer, the two-way controls and the evaluation script.
closes the privileged-state gap; the model already reads the layout to 2.39 mm on the evaluation seeds
trained on scripted-controller rollouts — the missing VLA the track scores
a 94–115 mm plate against a jaw that cannot both clear it and close on it
Run the bench on Core Ultra Series 2/3
one unchanged run turns NOT_THE_REQUIRED_MEASUREMENT into the measurement the track asks for
seeds, scorer and controls pinned, so a number reported against it stays comparable
Ordered by what the measurements say is blocking, not by what is easiest to demonstrate.
